verdict_reason: No material contradiction or important omission found in the exact summary for base/core multiplayer, 2–5 players. The numerical diagrams and procedures inspected agree with the summary.

scope.included: Recovered rulebook base/core multiplayer rules for 2–5 players, including setup, actions, costs and choices, control/movement/timing, all factions and mech abilities, combat/retreat, encounters, Factory, objectives, stars, immediate ending, scoring and tiebreaks.
excluded: Explicitly optional variants including Delay of Game
Outside-source FAQ, later revisions, external game knowledge
Bibliographic/frontmatter date and duration metadata authentication

independence.method: Read the complete exact summary, the complete 32-page extracted primary rulebook in full, and the PDF graphics necessary to recover icon-based quantities and procedures. Independently compared every gameplay section, with special attention to action timing, exceptions, and numerical scoring. Only communicated audit progress with the coordinating parent. Installed Python/PyMuPDF served solely as rendering dependencies.

method.source_page_numbering: Printed rulebook pages 1–32 correspond to PDF pages 1–32.
method.rendering: PyMuPDF, 1.5x page renders, saved only in the authorized source-assets directory.
graphic_checks: Board setup and starting placements/mat indicators (pp. 6–9)
Player Mat exposed cost, benefit, cube, structure and ongoing recruit icons (pp. 8–10, 12–14, 18, 20)
Production terrain/output chart, worker coverage, upgraded allowance (pp. 13–14)
One-time recruit quantities and ongoing Build example (pp. 9, 20); all four ongoing circle icons (p. 10)
All six structure bonus payout diagrams and adjacency example (p. 19)
Combat dial, combat-card distribution and worked battle (pp. 22–23)
End-priority text and full popularity scoring diagram (pp. 28–29)

decision_standard.PASS: No material rules contradiction or important omission in the scoped summary.
decision_standard.MINOR: A limited ambiguity or low-impact rules defect that does not broadly impair play.
decision_standard.MAJOR: A material rules error or important omission that can change legal decisions, timing, victory or scoring.

reviewed_claim_groups.subject: Scope, winning aim, components and overall flow
reviewed_claim_groups.assessment: Base/core multiplayer scope is explicit. Greatest final fortune wins; sixth star triggers immediate end; clockwise individual turns have no rounds. Listed faction piece quantities and roles agree with the source. The inventory lists 12 physical encounter tokens, while setup requires 11: the summary correctly specifies 11 placements rather than confusing these quantities.

reviewed_claim_groups.subject: Shared setup and seating
reviewed_claim_groups.assessment: Combat/encounter/objective decks are shuffled; Factory selection is player count plus one, face-down, with unseen remainder boxed; one random face-up structure tile; encounter markers on all 11 marked territories; resources/coins/multipliers supplied. Random faction and player mats and Nordic-Rusviet-Crimea-Saxony-Polania clockwise seating agree.

reviewed_claim_groups.subject: Player setup and public information
reviewed_claim_groups.assessment: Starting power/combat cards come from Faction Mat; popularity/coins/two objectives from Player Mat. Character, two land-adjoined starting workers, six remaining workers, mechs, cubes, structures, recruits, stars and action token are located correctly. One-time recruit spaces remain empty. Lowest numbered Player Mat starts. Secret card contents, public combat-card hand count with combat concealment, and coin-total disclosure rule agree.

reviewed_claim_groups.subject: Action selection, costs, gains and overlap
reviewed_claim_groups.assessment: Move the action token to a different section, optional top once then optional bottom once, including neither; Rusviet only waives the previous-section restriction. Full exposed red cost precedes optional exposed green benefit; top gains can pay bottom costs. Mat-specific variable costs and coins are properly delegated to the physical mat. Overlap of noninteractive bottom decisions preserves interactive resolution and end priority.

reviewed_claim_groups.subject: Control, resource use and home bases
reviewed_claim_groups.assessment: Units or an unopposed friendly structure control a territory and its resources; opposing units override structure control without acquiring abilities. Defender temporarily controls pending battle territory. Home bases are not territories; setup/retreat/Wayfare explain the exceptions. Resource types exclude workers, spending can draw from any controlled territories, and supply multipliers avoid a resource limit.

reviewed_claim_groups.subject: Normal movement, carrying and stopping
reviewed_claim_groups.assessment: Move up to two different units one adjacent territory, resolving sequentially, or take one coin. All units carry arbitrary resources, only mechs carry own workers, and carried-worker movement is distinct from the worker moving independently. Worker entry restrictions, enemy worker displacement/popularity loss, combat entry stops, character encounter stop, Speed and tunnel-step rules agree.

reviewed_claim_groups.subject: Rivers, lakes, printed tunnels and Mine movement
reviewed_claim_groups.assessment: Default river/lake prohibitions and the shoreline interpretation match. Printed tunnel adjacency is available to all units. Mine is personal, usable even under enemy control subject to entry/combat rules, and works for Factory movement. Lake worker/resource carriage constraints and faction-specific lake retreat distinction agree.

reviewed_claim_groups.subject: Bolster and Trade
reviewed_claim_groups.assessment: Bolster costs one coin and yields two power or one combat card before upgrades. Trade costs one coin and yields any two resources or one popularity, before upgrades. Resources require a controlled worker territory; all-workers-at-home exception is preserved. Monument/Armory benefits are assigned correctly, as is combat draw recycling/exhaustion.

reviewed_claim_groups.subject: Produce costs, outputs, workers and Mill
reviewed_claim_groups.assessment: Pay all currently exposed costs first; choose up to two controlled territories before upgrades; each worker there may produce one matching token. Mountain/metal, tundra/oil, farm/food, forest/wood, village/worker, lake/Factory/nothing match the diagram. New workers come left-to-right after payment; newly exposed costs apply to later Produce actions. Optional output and permanent workers agree. Mill adds a bonus territory and its own worker-equivalent output in addition to actual workers, including operation without an actual worker and only while controlled. Thus normal two-plus-Mill is three and upgraded three-plus-Mill is four.

reviewed_claim_groups.subject: Upgrade, Deploy and Build
reviewed_claim_groups.assessment: Oil/metal/wood correspond to Upgrade/Deploy/Build. Upgrade transfers any green cube to an empty bracketed red cost box, excluding solid borders. Deploy chooses any covered mech, placing it with a controlled worker, never on a lake, and unlocks the ability for character and all mechs. Build requires controlled worker territory, one structure of any owner per territory, permits Factory, excludes lakes/home, is permanent, and retains abilities despite enemy control except Mill.

reviewed_claim_groups.subject: Enlist, one-time and ongoing recruits
reviewed_claim_groups.assessment: Food cost; remove any recruit and place on any unused Faction Mat one-time space; immediately take the chosen two power/coins/popularity/cards, with permanent placement. The ongoing circle depends on the removed recruit section. Upgrade gives one power, Deploy one coin, Build one popularity, Enlist one card. Triggering players are self and immediate neighbors; two-player opponent triggers once; active-left-right order and sixth-star stop agree. Similar Factory actions and encounter benefits do not trigger ongoing bonuses.

reviewed_claim_groups.subject: Faction special abilities
reviewed_claim_groups.assessment: Swim is workers crossing rivers, excluding lakes; Relentless includes Factory; Coercion is one card as any one resource once per turn regardless of value; Dominate permits both starting objectives and more than two combat stars; Meander is up to two different options on one encounter in either order with first gain available for second cost. Correctly separates special abilities from mech unlocks.

reviewed_claim_groups.subject: Riverwalk and Speed for all factions
reviewed_claim_groups.assessment: Riverwalk destinations agree: Nordic/Saxony forest and mountain, Rusviet farm and village, Crimea farm and tundra, Polania village and mountain. Worker Swim is distinct from Nordic character/mech Riverwalk. All five have Speed, adding one territory to character/mech movement, with required stops overriding it.

reviewed_claim_groups.subject: Other faction mech abilities
reviewed_claim_groups.assessment: Underpass, Disarm, Township, People’s Army, Seaworthy, Artillery, Wayfare, Scout, Submerge and Camaraderie are individually preserved with relevant terrain/control, card, power, frequency and retreat restrictions. Polania combat-only popularity protection is correctly distinguished from undefended-worker displacement. Nordic adjacent-lake retreat exception is not incorrectly extended to Polania.

reviewed_claim_groups.subject: Combat commitment, reveal and payment
reviewed_claim_groups.assessment: Combat follows all movement and precedes following bottom action; attacker orders multiple battles and combat mech abilities. Zero power/popularity is allowed. Dial is limited to current power and seven; optional one card per character/mech plus eligible People’s Army card; simultaneous secret selection and reveal; attacker wins ties; both pay only dial power on track and discard all used cards face-up.

reviewed_claim_groups.subject: Combat result, retreat and awards
reviewed_claim_groups.assessment: Winner controls territory/resources and places an available combat star, with usual two-star limit and mandatory Saxony award. All losing units retreat, leaving all resources; Nordic exception retained. Winning attacker alone loses popularity per displaced enemy worker, including lake-carried workers; appropriate Polania exception retained. Loser draws one combat card only if some dial/card power was revealed. Pending attacks are undone upon sixth star.

reviewed_claim_groups.subject: Encounters
reviewed_claim_groups.assessment: Only character triggers and stops; resolve after full Move/all combats and before following bottom action if character remains. Lost contested entry preserves token. Show card/art and read capitalized thematic text; ordinary player must choose an affordable option, with optional benefit amount and Meander exception. All gained board pieces/resources go to encounter territory; no extra normal costs or benefits/recruit bonuses; card returns face-down to bottom. Factory Move follows the same rules.

reviewed_claim_groups.subject: Factory access, choice and use
reviewed_claim_groups.assessment: Each player’s character chooses exactly one permanent card on first completed Move there after required combat. Later visits cannot exchange it; other players may still obtain theirs. Fifth action section follows normal selection/top-bottom order and Rusviet exception; no related Player Mat bonuses. Factory Move selects one unit up to two territories or three for Speed character/mech; movement rules and Mine remain applicable.

reviewed_claim_groups.subject: Objectives, agreements and bribes
reviewed_claim_groups.assessment: Objectives reveal only during own turn before/after an action, with all requirements met then and optional delay. Star goes on objective track; completed and normally other card return to bottom of objective deck, with Saxony retaining second after first. Informal unenforceable agreements, coins-only tangible transfers, tournament coin prohibition and unavoidable initiated combat agree.

reviewed_claim_groups.subject: Star goals and immediate ending
reviewed_claim_groups.assessment: All achievement thresholds, permanence, ordinary one-award limits/two combat awards and Saxony exception agree. Sixth star ends immediately without equalizing turns. Bottom-action primary benefit, coins and own ongoing recruit benefit precede that action’s final star; neighbor power/popularity awards follow active action and active-left-right priority, stopping on an earlier sixth. Unresolved mixed-unit combat movement is returned rather than fought.

reviewed_claim_groups.subject: Final scoring and tiebreaks
reviewed_claim_groups.assessment: Held coins plus star, territory, resource-pair and selected structure bonus income agree. Popularity tiers are 0–6: 3/2/1; 7–12: 4/3/2; 13–18: 5/4/3. Factory contributes three territory counts, lakes count, home bases do not. Controlled resources are pooled into complete pairs, excluding workers/cards. Structure bonuses survive enemy control. Tie order is workers+mechs+structures, power, popularity, resources, territories, stars; character excluded.

reviewed_claim_groups.subject: All six structure bonus diagrams
reviewed_claim_groups.assessment: Visually checked every tile and its prose. Adjacent printed tunnels: 1/2–3/4–5/6 -> $2/$4/$6/$9; adjacent lakes or encounters: 1/2–3/4–5/6–7 -> $2/$4/$6/$9. Structures on printed tunnels: 1/2/3–4 -> $2/$4/$6. Longest continuous straight line and farms+tundras: 1/2/3/4 -> $2/$4/$6/$9. Each adjacent feature counts once; Mines do not become printed tunnel sites; removed encounter tokens still count; rivers do not break relevant adjacency/continuity. Summary’s complete payout table matches the graphics.

important_omission_assessment.assessment: The summary supplies all core procedures needed to select and pay actions, move and establish control, unlock faction abilities, resolve interactions, award stars, end immediately and determine the winner. Variable mat costs/start values remain on the actual mats, consistent with the source. No omitted core procedure was found.

acceptable_compression.omission: Exact inventory counts of shared cards, coin/resource tokens, multiplier tokens, reference cards and combat-card value distribution.
acceptable_compression.reason: These are inventory/reference/probability details; their omission does not change action legality or resolution, and the summary uses the real decks/mats rather than replacing them.

acceptable_compression.omission: Character backstories, designer notes, strategy tips, quick-start suggestions, sample scoring pause, achievement-sheet commemoration and contact/promotional material.
acceptable_compression.reason: Narrative, teaching or administrative content; sample scoring pause is expressly an example rather than actual scoring.

acceptable_compression.omission: Complete numerical transcription of every Player Mat’s starting values, costs and benefits.
acceptable_compression.reason: The source itself directs players to their randomly dealt physical mats and illustrates only examples. Summary correctly directs players to those exposed mat values and preserves default top-action values and all fixed recruit/structure quantities.

source_ambiguities_and_reconciliation.observation: Quick reference says objectives may be completed at any time, but the dedicated objective rule restricts reveal to own turn before/after top or bottom action.
source_ambiguities_and_reconciliation.audit_treatment: Used the dedicated rule; summary follows it.

source_ambiguities_and_reconciliation.observation: Combat winner paragraph mentions performing an encounter, while dedicated encounter rules explicitly defer until all combats finish.
source_ambiguities_and_reconciliation.audit_treatment: Used dedicated encounter sequencing; summary preserves all-combats-first timing.

source_ambiguities_and_reconciliation.observation: Example refers to 13–17 popularity level for a player at 18. Graphic visibly groups 13 through 18 at the top payout tier.
source_ambiguities_and_reconciliation.audit_treatment: Verified the graphic and example intention; summary correctly includes 18 in the top tier.

limitations: Audit is relative to the supplied recovered English rulebook only; it is not an assessment of later official revisions or FAQ rulings.

The source PDF illustrates selected mats/cards and is not a complete card or all-mat component gallery; mat-dependent quantities remain governed by the physical components as the source and summary specify.
Visual inspection targeted all gameplay diagrams needed for this assessment rather than every decorative illustration.
PASS concerns the scoped base/core rules summary, not frontmatter verification badges, linked-site availability or bibliographic metadata.
